carol: seeing a massive throughput drop on gpu-pool-7 since ~10:02UTC, a bunch of worker restarts and OOMs. rolling requests are getting 500s and latency spikes to 2x normal.
ben: copying logs? any common pattern in the OOM traces?
carol: pastes head of worker log: ```
E 10:03:12 worker[pid=4210] OOM: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
W 10:03:12 kernel_selector: switched kernel -> small-batch-fastpath
I 10:03:12 kv_cache: evicted 128 pages (pressure=0.87)
I 10:03:13 worker[pid=4210] restarting (crash loop count=3)
```
alice: ran perf profile on a repro run in staging — memory allocation hotspots show repeated allocations around kv-cache rehydration. looks like fragmentation (many small alloc/free patterns).
jordan: we pushed a kernel-selection heuristic change in the last rollout (PR #4621) that favors fastpath for batches < 6. could it be oscillating when eviction increases latency?
ben: that heuristic also changed prefetch/window behavior for the KV cache, right? iirc it shrinks prefetch when kernel=fastpath.
carol: yes, the prefetch window is reduced. i see kv cache miss spikes: `kv_miss_rate` jumped from 3% -> 42% at 10:02:58.
sre-oncall: alerting: noisy tenant r-tenant-14 showed a burst of small short calls around 10:01 that correlate with pool pressure.
jordan: that pattern fits: noisy tenant creates many small batches -> heuristic picks fastpath kernel + smaller prefetch -> kv misses increase -> more allocations for rehydration -> fragmentation -> OOMs and restarts. cascading effect.
carol: attaching quick metrics dump (summaries): ```
metric gpu_pool_7.throughput: -68%
metric worker_restarts.count: +14 in 15m
metric kv_cache.evictions: +900
metric avg_alloc_size: 48kb -> 12kb (more small allocs)
```
ben: can we temporarily pin kernel selection to the previous stable rule? rollback of PR #4621?
deploy-bot: rollback initiated: reverting kernel-selection heuristic (PR #4621) to main@c3a9f2. Estimated rollback ETA: 2m. :arrows_counterclockwise:
alice: while rollback is in progress, we should widen the prefetch window and bump kv cache target size on gpu-pool-7 to reduce rehydration churn. small patch: `kv.prefetch_window=64 -> 128`, `kv.target_pages += 25%`
carol: applied the kv adjustments to the pool via runtime flags; monitoring now.
ben: also throttle r-tenant-14 at the routing layer (rate-limit small requests) until we have a proper noisy-tenant mitigation. can SRE apply?
sre-oncall: put a soft limit of 50r/s for r-tenant-14 on pool-7. applied.
jordan: rollback completed on main; kernel logs show selection reverted to baseline at 10:05:07.
carol: early signs: kv_miss_rate back down to 6% and eviction spikes declining. worker restarts still trickling but no new OOMs in the last 90s. throughput beginning to recover.
alice: profile after rollback shows fragmentation still elevated; we need a short-term heap compaction experiment and a follow-up to improve allocation patterns for kv rehydration.
ben: agreed — immediate mitigation = rollback + kv window + noisy tenant throttle. schedule postmortem and a follow-up runbook to prevent heuristic oscillation.
carol: creating incident ticket and tagging eng-runtime + eng-ml for kernel heuristic review.
sre-oncall: good catch by monitoring + quick rollback. keeping page open for 30m for stability before closing. :white_check_mark:
carol: thanks all. saving logs to: s3://redwood-incidents/1768811223-memstripe-frag-surge/
ben: add benchmark: reproduce noisy small-batch burst in staging with artificial tenant to test heuristic under load.
alice: will prep a minim repro + perf trace; proposing a change: make kernel selection hysteresis-aware (require stable batch distribution for 10s before switching).
jordan: +1 for hysteresis and a longer prefetch ramp to avoid immediate oscillation.
carol: noted. will update incident ticket with action items. closing initial mitigation phase.
